Package io.webagent4j.browsercrawler

Record Class BrowserCrawlRequest

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
io.webagent4j.browsercrawler.BrowserCrawlRequest
Record Components:
browser - the already-launched browser this crawl runs within - the caller-supplied IBrowser instance IS the crawl's session boundary, not something BrowserCrawler creates or isolates itself. Cookies, storage, and authentication state already reachable through it are shared across every page this crawl opens, exactly as they would be for any other caller of the same IBrowser - if the caller reuses the same instance across multiple crawls (or alongside other automation on it), those crawls intentionally share that session state; isolating one crawl's session from another is the caller's responsibility. See docs/browser-crawler.md#session-model. The crawler owns only the IPage it creates and always closes it; browser itself is never closed by the crawler unless closeBrowserOnCompletion() is true.
seeds - absolute http/https URLs to start from, depth 0
maxDepth - the greatest depth a claimed navigation may have
maxPages - the greatest number of navigations this crawl may claim - enforced exactly by ClaimGate, which stays defensively synchronized even though, with maxConcurrency() pinned to 1, only one thread ever calls it
sameHostOnly - whether only the seeds' own hosts (not subdomains, unless includeSubdomains()) are in scope
includeSubdomains - whether subdomains of an in-scope host are also in scope
allowedHosts - additional hosts considered in scope, beyond the seeds' own hosts
navigationTimeout - the authoritative total budget for one navigation attempt - covering both the navigate() call itself (via IPage.navigate(String, java.time.Duration), not a backend's own default) and the subsequent stability wait, from a single monotonic deadline. Exceeded during navigation itself: BrowserCrawlFailureType.NAVIGATION_TIMEOUT; exceeded while waiting for stability: BrowserCrawlFailureType.PAGE_STABILITY_TIMEOUT
stabilityWindow - how long the page's DOM must report the same stability fingerprint before a page is considered stable - see docs/browser-crawler.md#stability
maxConcurrency - must currently be exactly 1. Neither IBrowser nor its pages are documented as thread-safe, and one caller-supplied IBrowser instance is the crawl session (cookies/storage/auth), so this engine navigates on a single execution lane - see docs/browser-crawler.md#concurrency-model. The field is kept, rather than removed, so a future phase that can honestly offer more than one lane (for example, one independent IBrowser per worker with an explicit session-sharing story) does not need a breaking API change to do it.
frameCrawlPolicy - which frames to discover links from, in addition to the top-level document - see FrameCrawlPolicy
queryParameterPolicy - how query parameters are normalized for the deduplication identity - reused unchanged from webagent4j-crawler-api
includeUrlPatterns - if non-empty, a discovered URL must match at least one pattern to be in scope
excludeUrlPatterns - a discovered URL matching any pattern is out of scope, checked after includeUrlPatterns()
failFast - whether a fatal page failure stops the crawl instead of being recorded and continuing
closeBrowserOnCompletion - whether the crawler closes browser() when the crawl ends (success, failure, or cancellation) - default false, respecting caller ownership
cancellationToken - the token this crawl observes; CancellationToken.cancel() may be called from any thread
public record BrowserCrawlRequest(IBrowser browser, List<URI> seeds, int maxDepth, int maxPages, boolean sameHostOnly, boolean includeSubdomains, Set<String> allowedHosts, Duration navigationTimeout, Duration stabilityWindow, int maxConcurrency, FrameCrawlPolicy frameCrawlPolicy, QueryParameterPolicy queryParameterPolicy, List<Pattern> includeUrlPatterns, List<Pattern> excludeUrlPatterns, boolean failFast, boolean closeBrowserOnCompletion, CancellationToken cancellationToken) extends Record
Immutable, fully validated configuration for one IBrowserCrawler.crawl(BrowserCrawlRequest) call.

Every invalid configuration fails at BrowserCrawlRequest.Builder.build(), never partway through a crawl. BFS is the only traversal strategy this phase implements - there is no traversalStrategy field to expose, unlike CrawlRequest, since a field accepting only one value adds surface without adding a real choice (see docs/browser-crawler.md#public-api-minimization).
